claims.text: The Planning Institute of Australia's PlanTech Best Practice Guidelines (adopted after the 2021 PlanTech principles and 2022 PlanTech Strategy) include a dedicated section on 'Artificial intelligence: Responsible and effective use', guiding planners on data governance, security and keeping humans in the loop. In 2026 PIA welcomed the Australian Government's national standards for AI infrastructure and released a Data Centres Guidance Note for planners and policy makers.

claims.scope: Voluntary professional-body guidance for Australian planners; not statute. Applies to PIA members, not a legal regulator.

claims.text: Jobs and Skills Australia's 'Our Gen AI Transition' Capacity Study (August 2025) scores occupations on augmentability and automatability (0-1, ILO-adapted) across 358 occupations; it finds augmentation outweighs automation economy-wide and that knowledge-intensive professional roles at ANZSCO Skill Levels 1-2 show the highest augmentation exposure. This occupation is a professional Skill Level 1 role, placing it in the high-augmentation, low-automation band.

claims.text: A 2025 Delphi study of 34 urban planners across Finnish municipalities (pop. >20,000) found planners commonly used Analytical AI to summarise plan information, report on environmental variables, and analyse and report on citizen feedback on draft plans, while flagging ethical, equity, accountability and privacy risks of AI in participatory planning.
